candidates.title: Ask to Distill: Learning to Synthesize Data for On-Policy Distillation
candidates.content: On-policy distillation (OPD) can succeed with surprisingly few training questions, motivating a view of questions as carriers of distributional knowledge transfer. How can we assess whether a newly generated question is valuable for distillation, and learn to generate better questions---without access to its correct answer? We introduce Ask-to-Distill (\method), a framework that treats synthetic questions as distribution elicitors and optimizes the teacher supervision they expose along student-generated trajectories. A student-initialized synthesizer is optimized using a distributional surrogate for question value, computed from a frozen student--teacher pair without reference answers, correctness rewards, or per-candidate student updates. The reward combines teacher--student disagreement with teacher probability mass on the student's candidate support, together with length and diversity controls. The generated questions are filtered and deduplicated into a prompt-only bank for standard OPD. candidates.title: ATEST: Adaptive Resource-Aware Test-Time Scaling for LLM Inference
candidates.content: Test-time scaling (TTS) improves large language model (LLM) reasoning by sampling multiple answers, but fixed sampling budgets ignore both query difficulty and the changing energy cost of inference under GPU contention. We measure up to a 4.1-fold increase in energy for the same four-sample query as GPU load rises. We present ATEST, a resource-aware TTS framework that jointly considers the expected value of additional samples and their current GPU cost. ATEST-Online, its default mode, requires no offline calibration: it incrementally generates samples, estimates the stability of the plurality answer, monitors live GPU conditions, and learns step energy cost online to decide when to stop. ATEST-Calibrated instead selects a per-query budget using offline accuracy and cost models, favoring deployments with stable loads. We evaluate both modes on four reasoning and question-answering datasets using Phi-3-mini on an NVIDIA A100 under controlled varying load, and test transfer to an NVIDIA L40S and Qwen2.5-3B. candidates.title: What Makes a Good Symbol for Hybrid Discrete-Continuous Planning?
candidates.content: The physical world has continuous state and action spaces, yet robot planning often benefits from hybrid discrete-continuous formulations that explicitly expose combinatorial structure, such as contact modes or discrete primitive actions. Existing methods typically rely on human-defined symbol sets or symbols derived from language supervision, without asking what makes a symbol computationally useful. In this paper, we take an inference-algorithm--centric view to define usefulness: a good symbol should expose the discrete commitments that simplify solving the original planning problem. We first introduce the concept of solver-sufficient symbolization by studying finite-horizon piecewise-affine systems, for which solver sufficiency can be precisely characterized, and develop a counterexample-guided algorithm for symbol invention. We then extend this principle to invent symbols for optimization objectives parameterized by general neural networks as energy functions, showing that solver-sufficient symbols can nevertheless be induced from their continuous optimization landscapes. candidates.title: TargetMITO: a rule-based model for generating functional synthetic mitochondrial targeting sequences in yeast
candidates.content: Abstract Mitochondria are essential organelles containing their own genomes, encoding a few proteins essential for energy production. Most of the mitochondrial proteins are nucleus-encoded, translated as precursors in the cytosol, with a large fraction of these precursors properly addressed by an N-terminal mitochondrial targeting sequence (MTS). These MTS share common features but no consensus sequence can explain their functionality nor the precursors-specific determinants of mitochondrial import. To help understand this mechanism, we created a simple computational model to generate functional synthetic MTS while maintaining a tight control on the design parameters. Using the budding yeast, we demonstrated the presence of precursors-specific import capabilities in addressing artificially nucleus-relocated OXPHOS proteins. Our research confirms the existence of cargo-dependent functional compatibilities and takes us one step closer towards improving gene therapy-based treatment of mitochondrial diseases.

candidates.title: Design of synthetic activators for programmable gene expression
candidates.content: Transcription factors control gene expression by recruiting transcriptional coactivators through intrinsically disordered transcriptional activation domains (TADs), whose weak and promiscuous interactions make it difficult to establish quantitative relationships between coactivator recruitment and transcriptional output, and to precisely modulate gene expression. To overcome this limitation, we set out to design coactivator-recruiting proteins using AlphaFold3-predicted TAD-coactivator interactions as a guide. We developed a high-throughput functional screening platform in mammalian cells and identified over 300 well folded nanomolar affinity binders to the transcription coactivators Mediator (multiple subunits), BRD4, NCOA, and p300; targeted interface mutations enabled systematic tuning of their binding affinities. Using a panel of p300 binders spanning nanomolar to micromolar affinities, we found an ultrasensitive relationship between coactivator-binding affinity and transcriptional output, with a sharp transcriptional activation threshold at ~500 nM. candidates.title: StoichRNA: A Scalable Framework to Map and Optimize Combinatorial RNA Systems at Single-Cell Resolution
candidates.content: RNA-based genetic cargos have emerged as versatile tools in both fundamental research and translational medicine, with growing applications in regenerative medicine, gene therapy, cell therapy, and vaccination. As the field advances beyond single-RNA delivery, coordinated engineering of multiple RNA species is enabling increasingly sophisticated and combinatorial biological functions. However, this shift raises a fundamental challenge: what combination and stoichiometry of RNA species should be delivered together to achieve a desired cellular function? As the number of RNA components increases, the design space expands combinatorially, making conventional optimization strategies labor-intensive and poorly scalable. Here, we introduce StoichRNA, a framework for scalable exploration of multi-RNA stoichiometry in a single experiment. Individual RNA species are delivered independently, each coupled to a distinct fluorescent marker that reports its intracellular abundance. Because uptake is stochastic, each cell acquires a unique combination and copy number of RNA components. candidates.title: VISAGENT: An Agent-Based End-to-End Voice Interaction System
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.26168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Voice-based public services have evolved from manual switchboards to intelligent platforms to meet modern user needs. However, current systems remain constrained by rigid menu-driven interaction, fragmented vertical services, and limited extensibility. To address these issues, we present VISAGENT, an agent-based end-to-end voice interaction system for large-scale public services that integrates end-to-end speech interaction, hierarchical agent routing, a scalable voice-agent marketplace, and user memory support. The system replaces menu-driven workflows with natural speech and dynamically dispatches user requests to either a general conversational model or specialized domain agents via a two-level routing paradigm that achieves sub-second intent-to-agent selection over hundreds of agents. User memory informs preference-aware agent selection and supplies relevant preferences and context to selected agents, supporting personalized task execution and reducing the need for users to repeat previously provided information. candidates.title: The Missing Compliance Class: LLM Graders That Collapse Jailbreak Success, and a Free Check
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.24872v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Jailbreak papers report an attack success rate, the share of responses that deliver the harmful request, and read it as a property of the target model. We hold the target model, the prompts and the responses fixed and change only the grader. Three dense graders of 8B and 9B parameters, from three model families, move compliant responses to the neighbouring class, evasion, instead of scattering them across classes. One of them assigns the compliance label zero times in 900 responses. This class collapse also appears on new harmful requests, on a target model from a third family, and in a held-out 7B grader from a fourth family. Per-class label counts expose it at no cost and without human labels. The collapse decides how the rate behaves under a change of grader. On two corpora of 900 responses and eight graders, the compliance rate differs by a factor of 22 to 25, while the non-refusal rate differs by 18 to 23 percentage points. Without the three collapsing graders, compliance differs by a factor of 1.7 to 2.8 on all four corpora, and non-refusal still differs by 10 to 22 points. candidates.title: How to Reduce Whisper Hallucination
candidates.content: arXiv:2609.32560v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Whisper is still what runs in production: one permissively licensed checkpoint, 99 languages, no per-language tuning. But it writes sentences nobody said. On 42 clips of pure room tone, whisper-large-v3 emits words on 61.9% of them and emits something on 100%. The usual response is to distil a student from Whisper pseudo-labels, filtering the hallucinations out of the corpus first, which deletes the evidence while leaving the behaviour in place: the student is fitted to the subset where the teacher was right, and inherits a failure mode absent from its own training data. The second response, adding non-speech audio so the model learns to stay quiet, already ships and works, but teaches suppression without discrimination. The checkpoint best on every non-speech arm here is also the one that recovers the fewest genuinely spoken phrases and deletes 58% of repeated speech. candidates.content: arXiv:2610.27256v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Analyzing merchant transaction histories requires dynamic temporal filtering, entity resolution, and aggregation over irregular event streams--operations poorly captured by static tabular or time-series forecasting benchmarks. We introduce TxnQA, an analytical QA benchmark comprising 27 task families (81 templates) alongside a 5-scenario fraud-risk reasoning suite that evaluates both verdicts and supporting evidence over synthetic, privacy-mitigated transaction data. Ground-truth answers are computed programmatically, and model performance is decomposed into format-following rate (FFR), conditional content accuracy (CA), and end-to-end correctness (E2E). candidates.content: arXiv:2610.27347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Checking whether a text complies with a body of law is slow when done by hand and fragile when done with keyword rules. This paper presents ComplianceAgent, the legal compliance sub-agent of COMPASS, a multi-agent framework that evaluates texts along four axes: digital sovereignty, carbon impact, compliance, and ethics. The agent relies on a large language model that scores a text on a fixed rubric, grounds its judgment in a reference legal corpus, and, when the score falls at or below a critical threshold, runs a corrective chain made of self-healing rewrites, a compliance label, an explainability report, and escalation to a human reviewer. We describe what the language model does at each step, how the memory of the agent is organized, and how the same implementation can be pointed at different reference corpora. We evaluate the agent in a Canadian and Quebec context, on a corpus of thirteen legal instruments that brings together federal and provincial texts, international treaties, and municipal documents of the City of Trois-Rivi\`eres. candidates.title: Runtime Control for AI Agents: Closing the Evaluation--Execution Gap in Operational Workflows
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.27480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language-model agents increasingly participate in operational workflows where approvals, binds, and payments create commitments. An approval valid when issued may no longer authorize execution after relevant facts, evidence, policy, or authority change. We call this the evaluation--execution gap. We specify a state-bound runtime assurance layer that separates probabilistic measurement from deterministic adjudication, binds an execution allowance to the decision-relevant basis of an approval, invalidates that allowance after relevant logged changes, and rechecks admissibility at dispatch. This distinguishes the continued validity of a prior approval from a current-state policy check. We describe eight failure modes, an assurance model, a reference architecture, and prospective interventions with retrospective remediation. In a scripted 42-case replay, the state-bound configuration identifies 15 later-invalidated approvals that a deliberately non-re-evaluating point-in-time comparator does not revisit; it holds 14 affected actions before dispatch and compensates one landed effect. candidates.title: Securing Agentic Commerce Through Behavior-Aware Fraud Detection and Cybersecurity for Trusted AI-Agent Payment Authorization
candidates.content: arXiv:2610.27483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing use of autonomous artificial intelligence agents in digital commerce creates new security concerns involving agent impersonation, unauthorized payments, compromised agents, and misuse of delegated authority. This research introduces the Autonomous Commerce Agent Guard System (ACAGS), a cybersecurity framework combining supervised machine learning, behavioral analytics, agent-specific authorization controls, and explainable AI. The framework was evaluated using synthetic financial transaction data augmented with simulated agent characteristics and five adversarial scenarios. XGBoost was selected following comparisons with alternative classifiers. Across ten experimental runs, behavioral features improved mean F1-score from 52.12% to 67.49%, with agent-specific features increasing performance to 69.46%. The framework achieved detection rates of 99.77% for abnormal agent behavior, 99.73% for impersonation, and 100% for malicious delegation and authorization-scope violations. candidates.content: arXiv:2610.27684v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Healthcare providers lose substantial revenue to systematic payer underpayments and claim denials, yet identifying the recurring, correctable patterns behind them remains largely manual and does not scale to hospital claim volumes. We present Pattern Intelligence, a deployed system that discovers such patterns without supervision by clustering claims on their adjudication behaviour rather than their identity. Each claim is embedded in a 130-dimensional vector combining per-line expected-versus-actual payment ratios, claim adjustment reason (CARC) codes, denial and payment signals, and service composition.
